target_moa.text: Maraviroc is a selective, slowly reversible small-molecule CCR5 co-receptor antagonist that binds human CCR5, preventing the interaction of HIV-1 gp120 with CCR5 and thereby blocking CCR5-tropic HIV-1 entry into cells.

citations.quote: SELZENTRY (maraviroc) is a selective, slowly reversible, small molecule antagonist of the interaction between human CCR5 and HIV-1 gp120. Blocking this interaction prevents CCR5-tropic HIV-1 entry into cells.
Maraviroc selectively binds to the human chemokine receptor CCR5 present on the cell membrane, preventing the interaction of HIV-1 gp120 and CCR5 necessary for CCR5-tropic HIV-1 to enter cells.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>8%) occurring more frequently than placebo were cough, pyrexia, upper respiratory tract infections, rash, musculoskeletal symptoms, abdominal pain, and dizziness. Serious concerns included hepatotoxicity (boxed warning) and cardiovascular events (myocardial ischemia/infarction) in 11 subjects (1.3%) on SELZENTRY vs none on placebo.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (>8% incidence) which occurred at a higher frequency compared to placebo are cough, pyrexia, upper respiratory tract infections, rash, musculoskeletal symptoms, abdominal pain, and dizziness (6).

Eleven subjects (1.3%) who received SELZENTRY had cardiovascular events including myocardial ischemia and/or infarction during the Phase 3 studies (total exposure 267 patient-years), while no subjects who received placebo had such events (total exposure 99 patient-years).
